newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso signs shipping register decree.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso signs shipping register decree.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Tuesday signed a decree that set regulations on foreign participation in coastal and river shipping, a lawmaker said on Tuesday.

The decree follows passage of a bill passed by Congress last year that creates the Special Brazilian Register for Maritime Navigation, Congressman Jose Carlos Aleluia, who drew up the legislation, told reporters.
Companies qualified for the register will pay less employer contributions than others and will be entitled to a low-interest credit line offered to the shipping sector by the Brazilian government.

Foreign shipping companies can qualify for the register if they are based in Brazil. Vessels must be manned by Brazilian captains and chief engineers, though the decree eliminated a previous stipulation that crews had to be two-thirds Brazilian.
